passage: I am Jyoti, and I was a guest at a wedding when Rehana, about two, ran to her mother and climbed onto her lap, arms wrapped round her neck, cheek pressed against her shoulder. Then a great-aunt stooped, saying, "Give me a kiss!" Rehana ducked behind her mother's arm. Her mother said, "She'll give you a high five if she wants." The great-aunt held up a hand. I couldn't tell what Rehana felt, but she did not seem upset.

qa.q: Where did Jyoti see Rehana?
qa.a: Jyoti saw Rehana at a wedding, as a guest.

qa.q: What does Rehana's ducking behind her mother's arm suggest, and what else could it be?
qa.a: It suggests she did not want a kiss from a relative she does not know well. She might also have been overwhelmed by the crowd.

qa.q: What did Rehana's mother do that adults can learn from?
qa.a: She offered the great-aunt a different way of greeting and did not force a kiss.

qa.q: How might the great-aunt feel about the refusal?
qa.a: She may feel a little put out at first, but a high five could still let her connect warmly with Rehana. 🙂

grounding: A toddler cuddles a familiar caregiver and may refuse a hug or kiss from a relative, and adults respect that.

passage: On Tuesday, Rekha came home from work and Charu, two, raised both arms until she was lifted, then rested her head under Rekha's chin. On Thursday an uncle visited and asked for a kiss; Charu shook her head and hid her face. "High five?" said Rekha. Charu slapped his palm and giggled. On Sunday Charu climbed onto Rekha's lap with a picture book and cuddled in, turning the pages herself.

qa.q: What did Charu do on Tuesday when Rekha came home?
qa.a: She raised both arms until Rekha lifted her, then rested her head under Rekha's chin.

qa.q: What might Charu's shaking her head at the uncle suggest, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: It suggests she did not want a kiss from him, though she was happy to join in when the choice was a high five. She might also have been tired or shy after the day.

qa.q: What did Rekha model by offering a high five?
qa.a: Rekha showed Charu her no would be heard, and gave the uncle another way to say hello. 🙂

qa.q: How might the uncle feel about the high five?
qa.a: He may feel relieved to have another way to connect, and understand that Charu is simply not ready for kisses.

grounding: A toddler seeks cuddles from a familiar caregiver and has the right to refuse a kiss from a relative.

passage:
At the family function in Chennai, Sunaina kept climbing back into her mother Sharmila's lap for cuddles, pressing her cheek to Sharmila's chest.
An uncle leaned over. "Give me a kiss, Sunaina!"
Sunaina turned her face away and clung tighter.
"She's not in the mood," said Sharmila lightly. "Maybe a wave?"
The uncle straightened up. "Okay, okay. A wave then." Sunaina peeped out and waved.

qa.q: Where did Sunaina keep climbing for cuddles?
qa.a: Into her mother Sharmila's lap.

qa.q: What was Sunaina feeling when she turned her face away from the uncle?
qa.a: She didn't want to kiss him, perhaps feeling shy or uncomfortable, while she felt safe and loving with her mother.

qa.q: Which choice of Sharmila's respected Sunaina, and why?
qa.a: Saying lightly that she wasn't in the mood and offering a wave respected Sunaina's right to refuse a kiss.

qa.q: How might the uncle feel when Sunaina turns away?
qa.a: He might feel a little disappointed, but he accepts the wave without fuss.

grounding: A toddler seeks cuddles from her mother but refuses a relative's kiss, and her mother respects that.

passage:
"Bye, Santosh! Give Bua a big kiss!" said Ira, bending down.
Santosh stepped back and put his hands behind his back.
"Ask him, Ira didi," said his mother. "Santosh, kiss for Bua?"
"No."
"Okay," said Ira. "High five, then?"
Santosh grinned and slapped her hand. Then he ran to his mother and threw both arms round her legs for a long cuddle.

qa.q: What did Santosh give Ira instead of a kiss?
qa.a: A high five.

qa.q: What was Santosh feeling when he put his hands behind his back?
qa.a: He didn't want to give a kiss and felt uncomfortable being asked; he felt happy once he could say goodbye his own way.

qa.q: What did his mother and Ira do that respected Santosh?
qa.a: They asked him first and accepted his "no", then offered a high five instead.

qa.q: How might Ira feel about the high five?
qa.a: She seems cheerful and fine with it, glad to still share a goodbye.

grounding: A toddler refuses an aunt's kiss, and the family respects it and offers a high five instead.

passage: Daycare note, Wednesday. Baljeet is a great cuddler. After nap he climbed into my lap and snuggled for a long time, and he hugs his friends at goodbye. Today, though, a visiting grandparent of another child bent to kiss him. He pulled back and turned away. I said, "He doesn't want a kiss today," and offered a wave. She understood and waved. Baljeet waved back. Tanuja, daycare teacher

qa.q: When did Baljeet climb into Tanuja's lap?
qa.a: After nap.

qa.q: What was Baljeet feeling when he pulled back from the visitor?
qa.a: He was likely uncomfortable with a kiss from someone he didn't know well, even though he loves cuddles with familiar people.

qa.q: Which choice of Tanuja's worked, and why?
qa.a: Speaking up for him and offering a wave worked, because it respected his refusal and kept things friendly.

qa.q: How might the visiting grandparent feel?
qa.a: She might feel a little surprised, but she understood and waved.

grounding: A teacher notes a toddler's love of cuddles and respects his refusal of a visitor's kiss.

passage:
At the family gathering in the small town, Saurabh clung to Anjali all afternoon, cuddled on her lap, reaching up whenever she stood.
Then his Bua swept in. “Give me a kissy, Saurabh!” She leaned in.
Saurabh turned his face away and pressed into Anjali's shoulder.
“He doesn't want to right now, Didi,” said Anjali. “Maybe a wave?”
Bua's face fell for a second, then she laughed. Saurabh gave her a tiny wave from his mother's arms.

qa.q: Who swept in and asked for a kiss?
qa.a: His Bua swept in and asked for a kissy.

qa.q: What was Saurabh feeling when he turned away from his Bua's kiss?
qa.a: He felt shy and unsure in the busy gathering, wanting to stay close to his mother, and did not want to be kissed right then.

qa.q: Why was Anjali's answer a wise one?
qa.a: It respected Saurabh's right to refuse a kiss while offering a friendly wave instead, which kept things warm with Bua.

qa.q: How did Bua feel when Saurabh turned away?
qa.a: Her face fell for a second, showing she was a little hurt, but she laughed it off.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler cuddling and seeking his mother, and an adult respecting his right to refuse a relative's kiss.
